Fixes the fault that handed a player the starting kit again after every join, and left those starting items stuck and unusable in the hotbar.

## Server

### Fixed
- A player's save is now keyed to their character name rather than to the name the game derives from their machine. A client cannot send its character name until it has finished loading the world, about a minute after it connects, so the server locked the save to the machine-derived name it saw first and then ignored the real character name when it arrived. The alias table that exists to heal this refused to record the very case it was written for, because a machine-derived name of the form `Name_Surname-07088ACA40` reads as a launcher identity. It records that case now, and honours it, so the next session keys to the character from its first tick. Identity is still never reissued mid-session; that resets inventory ownership.
- The inventory apply path now finds owner-id members that Blueprint stores under a mangled name (`Name_Index_GUID`), which no exact-name lookup can match. Without that write the inventory was never bound to the player's saved data, which is what returned the starting kit on each join and left those items visible but unusable.
- When no owner field matches even then, the server records the parameter's real field list once instead of failing silently, so the cause is named rather than guessed at.

### Changed
- Property enumeration behind the two fixes above runs at most once per process, and only after the exact-name lookup has already missed. Broad enumeration stays off everywhere else.
